headline: Apple Sets New iPhone Sales Record Despite No Standard Model Release
summary: iPhone revenue soared 17% year-over-year to $57.58 billion, driven by Pro models and price increases, even as Apple launched its first foldable phone.
details: Apple announced a record-breaking quarter for iPhone sales, with revenue jumping 17% to $57.58 billion. This surge occurred despite the absence of a new standard iPhone model in the latest refresh, with sales driven by the pricier iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, alongside price hikes on older models.

The company also introduced its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, though its preorder sales will not be reflected in this earnings report. Apple CEO John Ternus noted that while memory costs were higher, they were offset by inventory benefits and lower costs on other components.

Overall, Apple reported a 12% increase in revenue, reaching $114.5 billion. The Mac business saw a 24% growth to $10.79 billion, and the services division, including the App Store and subscriptions, expanded to $31.57 billion. However, iPad revenue saw a 10% decline, with $6.23 billion in sales.

In addition to the iPhone, Apple has expanded its product lineup with a smart home push, including smart displays, video doorbells, security cameras, and door locks developed in partnership with LG and Schneider Electric. They also recently unveiled a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen, a feature previously resisted by executives.
